summary.whatChanges: Accept-header parsing now recognizes an uppercase `Q` quality parameter, falling back to `params.Q` when `params.q` is absent, so quality values and the resulting sort order are honored regardless of the parameter's letter case. Tests cover both parsing and sorting.
behaviorChanges: `Accept: text/html;Q=0.5` now yields q=0.5 instead of defaulting to 1
Media types with uppercase `Q` are ordered correctly by quality during content negotiation
`Q=0` now correctly marks a media type as unacceptable (q=0)
The params object still stores the original casing (`params.Q`), so the raw key is unchanged
risks: Only exact `q` and `Q` are handled; the params map keeps original casing, so consumers reading `params.q` directly still miss uppercase headers
If a header sends both `q` and `Q`, lowercase silently wins with no error
Clients previously treated as q=1 for uppercase Q may now be deprioritized or excluded, changing negotiated response types
